headline: High-risk shared-workspace and output-trust pathways: CrewAI can write/exfiltrate while Khoj reads indexed notes, creating medium prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can write files and run tools in a shared working directory, while Khoj reads indexed documents and notes. If CrewAI outputs attacker-controlled content into files that Khoj later ingests, Khoj may treat it as trusted context. No shared channel is explicit, so this is not high, but the pathway exists.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes content into a directory that Khoj indexes or reads
IF Khoj ingests file text as conversational context without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate CrewAI and Khoj into different directories
Disable automatic indexing of CrewAI output folders
Add provenance tags to files before Khoj ingests them
Review any file-based handoff before Khoj reads it

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and secrets, and has broad network egress; Khoj indexes personal notes and documents and can call external APIs. If they share a workspace or CrewAI writes sensitive outputs into files Khoj indexes, sensitive data can flow into Khoj's retrieval and outward through its API-backed chat path. The shared-workspace risk is plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF CrewAI stores secrets or sensitive crew data in files under Khoj's indexed corpus
IF Khoj is configured to use cloud or external search providers
mitigations: Keep sensitive CrewAI artifacts outside Khoj's indexed corpus
Turn off external search providers for sensitive sessions
Use separate OS users or containers for the two agents
Redact secrets before any file handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Khoj can read the filesystem and maintains a shared index across clients. They do not both have write access, so the high-severity same-directory write conflict is not supported. Still, overlapping access to shared mutable files or indexes can cause races and stale state in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or index store
IF CrewAI writes files while Khoj reindexes or reads them concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate storage roots
Serialize writes before Khoj reindexing
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Run each agent under a separate OS account

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate tool outputs and intermediate facts, and Khoj is a retrieval/chat system that may surface those artifacts to users. If Khoj treats CrewAI-produced text as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream answers or actions. The profiles do not prove automatic action-taking, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF CrewAI-produced text is ingested into Khoj retrieval or chat context
IF Khoj presents retrieved CrewAI output without a verification step
mitigations: Mark CrewAI outputs as untrusted in metadata
Require human review before Khoj surfaces CrewAI-derived claims
Add a verification step for retrieved facts
Separate raw outputs from user-facing notes

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Khoj indexes personal notes and documents and may use cloud or configured search providers. If personal or regulated data from CrewAI is indexed by Khoj and then sent to external providers, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data from CrewAI is stored in Khoj's indexed notes
IF Khoj forwards that data to a cloud provider or external search service
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Khoj indexing
Use self-hosted-only providers for sensitive content
Set short retention on indexed artifacts
Document a data-handling boundary between the two systems
